knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)

```{r load libraries, include=FALSE}
library(tidyverse)
library(pwr)
library(Superpower) # Daniël Lakens power package
#devtools::install_github("arcaldwell49/Superpower") #to get his package
```

```{r load data and calculate beta, include=FALSE}
options(scipen=999)

load("clean_task_data.2020.27.12.RData") 
Neuroethics_Judgement %>% 
dplyr::select(user_id,risk,gain,condition, experimental_treatment_selected) %>%
  group_by(user_id) %>% #group by user id
  mutate(risk.c = scale(risk, scale = F)) %>% #mean center variables
  mutate(gain.c = scale(gain, scale = F)) %>% 
  mutate(treatment = ifelse(experimental_treatment_selected == "Yes to treatment", 1, 0))  -> logit.data 

m.logit <- by(logit.data, logit.data$user_id, function(x) glm(treatment ~ risk.c*gain.c, data = x, family = binomial(link = "logit")))
#here is the code that I use to get the subjects

##extract subject betas 
n = nrow(logit.data)/75
user_id <- names(m.logit)
betas <- list()
colin <- list()

for (i in 1:n){
dat = m.logit[[i]]$coefficients
  betas[[i]] = dat
}
subjectModels <- do.call(rbind, betas)
colnames(subjectModels) <-  c('Intercept', 'Risk_Beta', 'Gain_Beta', 'Interaction')
subjectModels <- cbind.data.frame(user_id, subjectModels)

#check the variance inflation factors 
for (i in user_id){
vif <- car::vif(m.logit[[i]])
colin[[i]] <- vif
}

subjectcolin <- as.data.frame(do.call(rbind, colin))
subjectcolin <- tibble::rownames_to_column(subjectcolin, "user_id")

#remove subject if they have vif for risk or gain above 4 
subjectcolin %>% 
  filter(!risk.c > 4) %>% 
  filter(!gain.c > 4) -> index 

#merge the subject models extracted above and the index
subjectModels <- merge(subjectModels, index, "user_id")

#create data that only contains subjects after VIF data exculsion
data <- merge(logit.data, subjectModels, "user_id")
data %>% 
   dplyr::select(c("user_id","condition","Risk_Beta", "Gain_Beta")) %>% 
  distinct() -> data 
```


**Compute power for a One Factor ANOVA with seven levels**
```{r power analysis,}
data %>%
  group_by(condition) %>%
  summarize(n = n(),
            mean = mean(Risk_Beta),
            sd = sd(Risk_Beta)) %>% na.omit() -> X

string <- "7b" #7 groups, one for each cog domain
n <- 45 
# Say we are thinking of running 45 people in each condition (this is the average we currently gathered)
mu <- X$mean #extract the Risk_Beta means for each condition
# Enter means in the order that matches the labels below.
sd <- mean(X$sd) #use a single standard deviation to not break the assumption of equal variance
labelnames <- c("condition", "Attention (Concentration)", "Language (spoken)", "Long Term Memory", "Mood", "Motor Function", "Self-control", "Short Term (Working) Memory") #
# the label names should be in the order of the means specified above.
design_result <- ANOVA_design(design = string,
                   n = n,
                   mu = mu,
                   sd = sd,
                   labelnames = labelnames)
alpha_level <- 0.05 #conventional

monte_result1 <- ANOVA_power(design_result,
                             alpha_level = 0.05,
                             verbose = FALSE,
                             emm = TRUE,
                             contrast_type = "pairwise",
                             emm_p_adjust = "holm", #mutiple comparisons adjust
                             nsims = 10000, #set total number of simulations 
                             seed = 235353) #set seed for reproducibility

exact_result <- ANOVA_exact(design_result,
                            alpha_level = alpha_level,
                            verbose = FALSE)

knitr::kable(exact_result$main_results, caption = "Exact ANOVA Results") 
knitr::kable(monte_result1$main_results, caption = "Simulated ANOVA Results")

#showing it again with pwr package to check
K <- 7
n <- 45
f <- exact_result$main_results$cohen_f
pwr.anova.test(n = n,
               k = K,
               f = f,
               sig.level = alpha_level)$power
```
This analysis tells us that running the study with 45 participants in each condition is very likely to not yield a significant test result, even if our expected pattern of differences is true. 

Let’s explore which pattern of means we would need to expect to have 90% power for the ANOVA with 45 participants in each group. 
```{r}
#now simulate a 90% power
K <- 7
n <- 45
sd <- mean(X$sd)
r <- 0
#Calculate f when running simulation
f <- pwr.anova.test(n = n,
                    k = K,
                    power = 0.9,
                    sig.level = alpha_level)$f
f
f2 <- f^2
ES <- f2 / (f2 + 1) #calcuate eta-squared
ES
```
So, at least based on Cohen's benchmarks, we have 90% power to detect effects that are slightly below a medium effect benchmark (`f`).
Expressed in eta-squared, we can detect values of `ES` or larger. 

```{r}
#calculate optimal n for 90% power given what we observed
plot_power(design_result, min_n = 10, max_n = 250)

#look at comparisions with 71 per conditions
n <- 71
design_result <- ANOVA_design(design = string,
                   n = n, 
                   mu = mu, 
                   sd = sd, 
                   labelnames = labelnames,
                   plot = FALSE) #do not print the plot (same as above)

exact_result2 <- ANOVA_exact(design_result,
            emm = TRUE)
knitr::kable(exact_result2$main_results, caption = "71 per condition ANOVA Results") 
knitr::kable(exact_result2$pc_results, caption = "71 pairwise comparisons Results") 

n <- 150
design_result <- ANOVA_design(design = string,
                   n = n, 
                   mu = mu, 
                   sd = sd, 
                   labelnames = labelnames,
                   plot = FALSE) #do not print the plot (same as above)

exact_result3 <- ANOVA_exact(design_result,
            emm = TRUE)
knitr::kable(exact_result3$main_results, caption = "150 per condition ANOVA Results") 
knitr::kable(exact_result3$pc_results, caption = "150 pairwise comparisons Results") 


monte_result2 <- ANOVA_power(
  design_result,
  alpha_level = 0.05,
  verbose = FALSE,
  emm = TRUE,
  contrast_type = "pairwise",
  emm_p_adjust = "holm",
  nsims = 10000, #set total number of simulations
  seed = 7543) #set seed for reproducibility

knitr::kable(monte_result2$main_results)
knitr::kable(monte_result2$pc_results, caption = "Simulatation 150 per condition ANOVA Results")
```

With 71 participants per condition, power for this simple comparison is varies. If we want to aim for 90% power for follow up tests, we need more participants. 150 participants provides good power for the follow-up comparison between our conditions. But power for the difference between conditions for long-term memory and self control is incredibly low. We would need alot more participants to have 90% power for those comparisons (I did over 100000 subjects per condition, so something is suspect.)


**Note** that this power analyses is bias given that I used the pilot data to make these estimate see citation below for more on that. 



Albers, Casper, and Daniël Lakens. 2018. “When Power Analyses Based on Pilot Data Are Biased: Inaccurate Effect Size Estimators and Follow-up Bias.” Journal of Experimental Social Psychology 74: 187–95. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jesp.2017.09.004.


```{r archive graphs, eval=FALSE, include=FALSE}
nsims = 10000
library(Superpower)
library(pwr)
library(tidyverse)
library(viridis)

data %>%
  group_by(condition) %>%
  summarize(n = n(),
            mean = mean(Risk_Beta),
            sd = sd(Risk_Beta)) %>% na.omit() -> X

string <- "7b" #7 groups, one for each cog domain
n <- 45 
# Say we are thinking of running 45 people in each condition (this is the average we currently gathered)
mu <- X$mean #extract the Risk_Beta means for each condition
# Enter means in the order that matches the labels below.
sd <- mean(X$sd) #use a single standard deviation to not break the assumption of equal variance
labelnames <- c("condition", "Attention (Concentration)", "Language (spoken)", "Long Term Memory", "Mood", "Motor Function", "Self-control", "Short Term (Working) Memory") #
# the label names should be in the order of the means specified above.
design_result <- ANOVA_design(design = string,
                   n = n,
                   mu = mu,
                   sd = sd,
                   labelnames = labelnames)
alpha_level <- 0.05 #conventional

p_a <- plot_power(design_result,
                  max_n = 200)
p_a$power_df$effect <- 0

design_result <- ANOVA_design(design = string,
                              n = n, 
                              mu = c(0,0,0,0.1), 
                              sd = 1, 
                              labelnames = labelnames)
p_b <- plot_power(design_result,
                  max_n = 100)

p_b$power_df$effect <- 0.1

design_result <- ANOVA_design(design = string,
                              n = n, 
                              mu = c(0,0,0,0.2), 
                              sd = 1, 
                              labelnames = labelnames)
p_c <- plot_power(design_result,
                  max_n = 100)

p_c$power_df$effect <- 0.2

design_result <- ANOVA_design(design = string,
                              n = n, 
                              mu = c(0,0,0,0.3), 
                              sd = 1, 
                              r = 0.5, 
                              labelnames = labelnames)
p_d <- plot_power(design_result,
                  max_n = 100)

p_d$power_df$effect <- 0.3

design_result <- ANOVA_design(design = string,
                              n = n, 
                              mu = c(0,0,0,0.4), 
                              sd = 1, 
                              r = 0.5, 
                              labelnames = labelnames)
p_e <- plot_power(design_result,
                  max_n = 100)

p_e$power_df$effect <- 0.4

design_result <- ANOVA_design(design = string,
                              n = n, 
                              mu = mu, 
                              sd = 1, 
                              r = 0.5, 
                              labelnames = labelnames)
p_f <- plot_power(design_result,
                  max_n = 100)

p_f$power_df$effect <- 0.5


plot_data <- rbind(p_a$power_df, p_b$power_df, p_c$power_df, 
                   p_d$power_df, p_e$power_df, p_f$power_df)%>%
  mutate(AxB = `A:B`) %>% select(n,effect,A,B,AxB)

long_data = plot_data %>%
  gather("A", "B", "AxB", key = factor, value = power)

plot1 <- ggplot(long_data, aes(x = n, y = power,color = as.factor(effect))) +
  geom_line(size = 1.5) +
  scale_y_continuous(breaks = seq(0,100,10)) +
  labs(color = "Effect Size",
       x = "Sample Size per Group",
       y = "Power (%)") +
  scale_color_viridis_d() + facet_wrap( ~ factor, ncol=2)
```
